issues.title: Early HT capacity adaptation when groups slightly exceed initial sink capacity
issues.hypothesis: With >2 threads, RadixHTConfig::SinkCapacity() gives each thread a 32768-slot aggregate HT, so it resizes at ResizeThreshold = 21845 entries. DecideAdaptation(), the only thing that can grow the HT, runs only once a thread has sunk ADAPTIVITY_THRESHOLD = 1,048,576 rows. q16 puts ~1.18M rows into 27,839 groups (above 21845). In the distinct-finalize phase (HashAggregateDistinctFinalizeTask::AggregateDistinctGrouping, which sinks into grouping_data.table_data.Sink), each of the 8 tasks gets ~150k rows covering nearly all groups. No thread reaches 1M rows, so the HT never grows. It fills and is Abandon()ed about 7 times per thread, materialising many copies of each group, and RadixPartitionedHashTable finalize then has to combine several hundred thousand rows instead of ~27k per thread. Measured: the same join with a plain GROUP BY brand,type,size count() takes 178 ms, against 121 ms without the GROUP BY. That is ~60 ms for 1.18M rows into 27k groups, ~400 ns/row of CPU, which is pathological. count(DISTINCT) adds ~45 ms more through the same path.
issues.plan: In src/execution/radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp, RadixPartitionedHashTable::Sink: just after the `if (ht.Count() + STANDARD_VECTOR_SIZE < ResizeThreshold(local_sink_capacity)) return;` early-out (the HT is full) and before the Abandon() call, add an early check that can only grow the HT. Conditions: !lstate.adapted && gstate.number_of_threads > GROW_STRATEGY_THREAD_THRESHOLD (so HLL is enabled) && !gstate.external && lstate.local_sink_capacity < ADAPTIVITY_THRESHOLD && ht.GetSinkCount() >= 2 * ResizeThreshold(local_sink_capacity), so there are enough samples. Compute deduplicated_count = ht.GetMaterializedCount(), hll_count = MinValue(ht.GetHLLUpperBound(), deduplicated_count) and the same percentages as DecideAdaptation. If deduplicated_pct / hll_pct > 2.0 (CAPACITY_INCREASE_DEDUPLICATION_RATE_THRESHOLD), set new_capacity = MinValue(GetCapacityForCount(hll_count), ADAPTIVITY_THRESHOLD). If new_capacity > local_sink_capacity, set lstate.local_sink_capacity = new_capacity, call ht.Abandon(); ht.Resize(new_capacity); and return. Do not set adapted, so the existing 1M-row DecideAdaptation still runs later, and do NOT take the SkipLookups branch early. Best done as a small helper next to DecideAdaptation, perhaps sharing the math. Memory per thread stays bounded by the existing ADAPTIVITY_THRESHOLD cap. Also check the MaybeRepartition path that follows, which must still run when no resize happens.
issues.expected_gain: q16: 10-20% (the main-HT sink and finalize in count(DISTINCT) finalize, ~27k groups). Any hash GROUP BY with roughly 22k-700k groups and fewer than 1M rows per thread gains similarly.
issues.generality: Any parallel hash aggregation whose group count exceeds the initial 32k-slot capacity but whose per-thread input is below 1M rows. That is common for medium-cardinality GROUP BYs on joins or filtered scans, and in the count(DISTINCT) finalize phase. Possible slowdowns: inputs where the HLL early sample overestimates the dedup benefit (cost: a larger HT, at most the existing cap), and a slightly larger per-thread HT that falls out of L2.
issues.risk: Low. The change can only grow capacity, within existing caps, using the same mechanism DecideAdaptation already uses (Abandon + Resize), so correctness is unaffected. External/out-of-core mode is excluded. The 2-thread grow strategy is untouched.

issues.title: Perfect hash join for sparse-but-bounded key ranges
issues.hypothesis: q16's inner join on ps_partkey = p_partkey has a 296k-row build side with key range ~2M. PerfectHashJoinExecutor::CanDoPerfectHashJoin rejects it because MAX_BUILD_SIZE = 1048576 (absolute range cap). The probe takes 0.25 s cumulative for 1.24M probe rows (~200 ns/row per thread) and is the largest operator after the aggregate. A perfect HJ replaces hash, pointer chase and key compare with a direct index.
issues.plan: In src/execution/operator/join/perfect_hash_join_executor.cpp CanDoPerfectHashJoin, allow build_range up to a larger cap (e.g. 4M) when the density ht.Count()/build_range is at least ~1/8, keeping the existing 1M absolute cap otherwise. Check the memory estimate (build_size * sum of rhs column widths) against the temporary memory or available memory. FullScanHashTable is single-threaded, so measure the build cost.
issues.expected_gain: q16 ~5-10% if the probe gets 2x faster.
issues.generality: Joins on integer surrogate keys whose build side is filtered (a dense domain with a selective filter on the dimension). Possible slowdowns: memory overhead and the single-threaded build for wide build payloads.
issues.risk: Medium. Memory amplification (range * row width) and the single-threaded build could hurt larger builds. Needs a memory guard.

issues.title: Enforce pushed IN-list filter in scan instead of mark join
issues.hypothesis: The part scan emits 1.86M rows that the `optional: p_size IN (...)` filter does not reduce. InClauseRewriter (src/optimizer/in_clause_rewriter.cpp) turns IN lists with >=6 constants into a MARK join + FILTER, and the scan applies only an optional zonemap filter. A scan-level IN filter would cut the scan output to 296k and remove the mark join.
issues.plan: Investigate why the pushed IN filter is optional (filter pushdown of IN to TableFilter) and whether constant IN lists of moderate size (< some N) on scan columns could stay as an IN expression filter evaluated in the scan instead of the mark join rewrite.
issues.expected_gain: q16 small (~2-4%): build-side pipeline ~0.13 s cumulative.
issues.generality: Any scan with a constant IN list of 6+ values.
issues.risk: Low-medium. Optimizer change; plan shapes change for many queries.

## Memory (gen1 round1)

### Workload
- Only template q16: partsupp JOIN part (filtered: brand<>, type NOT LIKE prefix, size IN 8 consts) + NOT IN (supplier LIKE) mark join, GROUP BY brand,type,size count(DISTINCT suppkey), ~27.8k groups, ~1.18M rows into agg. Bench ~180 ms.
- Time split (EXPLAIN ANALYZE totals, round 1): join only count(*) 82 ms; join + payload max() no group 121 ms; + GROUP BY plain count 178 ms; with count(DISTINCT) ~222 ms (profile). So aggregation is ~100 ms, join+scans ~120 ms.
- Profile operator cumulative: HASH_GROUP_BY 0.47 s, inner HASH_JOIN probe 0.19-0.25 s, partsupp scan (with BF dynamic filter) 0.17-0.26 s, part scan 0.10 s (emits 1.86M rows; IN filter is only 'optional', applied by MARK join afterwards).

### Codebase facts
- Radix aggregate HT (src/execution/radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp): with >2 threads the sink capacity is 32768 (resize threshold 21845 at LOAD_FACTOR 1.5). The HT is Abandon()ed when full. DecideAdaptation (grow capacity / SkipLookups) runs only after ADAPTIVITY_THRESHOLD = 1M rows per thread, so medium-cardinality aggs never adapt.
- count(DISTINCT) path (physical_hash_aggregate.cpp): sinks only the distinct radix table (keys = groups + distinct col), and CanSkipRegularSink holds when all aggs are distinct. HashAggregateDistinctFinalizeTask then scans the distinct partitions and Sinks into the main table_data via the same RadixPartitionedHashTable::Sink, so it hits the same capacity logic.
- Compressed materialization: p_brand (8 chars) -> uhugeint, p_type (25 chars) stays VARCHAR (non-inlined), p_size -> utinyint.
- Perfect HJ gate: perfect_hash_join_executor.cpp CanDoPerfectHashJoin, absolute MAX_BUILD_SIZE = 1048576 range, INNER only, single integer key.
- InClauseRewriter: IN lists with >=6 constants become a MARK join against a COLUMN_DATA_SCAN.
- dbe-tool: no pipes or greps allowed in bash. Use `dbe-tool sql "EXPLAIN ANALYZE ..."` for quick variant timing (the Total Time line is at the top).

### Experiments
- R1 dispatched: early HT capacity growth (grow-only, HLL-based, once sink_count >= 2x resize threshold). Pending.

### Backlog ideas
- Perfect HJ for sparse-bounded range (density gate, memory guard).
- Enforce the IN-list filter in the scan instead of the mark join (small).
- Distinct HT for near-unique data: early SkipLookups (risky to decide on a small sample; prior thinking says small gain).
- String group keys pointing into the join build heap cause random reads during hash and compare (unverified).

### Prior-run notes (other workloads, see MEMORY index): perfect HJ / large perfect HA gave ~20% on q13; FSST decode laziness etc. Not directly applicable here.
